analysis:
Examined both modified files, Serve metadata/patch and all supplied surrounding source against the indexed threat model and detailed T-041 evidence. Capacity adds superviseServingAuthorization() at head line 82, after several awaited maintenance operations. Serve records disconnected state before event processing (head line 300), records connected/disconnected transitions in the fast connection-control reader (head line 426), and records disconnection when the stream ends (head line 436). Existing authorization clearing and App Attest cancellation remain, separate from slow work FIFO processing. Registration still binds the process encryption key and captures signed runtime claims; no supplied change alters encryption, token handling, cache scope, at-rest crypto, billing or privileged-helper authority. No independently supported regression was identified.
Integration must examine the new helper implementations and their state consumers: noteCoordinatorConnection, event.isConnected and superviseServingAuthorization are not supplied here. Verify that connection bookkeeping cannot reuse stale grants or treat connectivity as serving permission (A-016, T-052/T-053, TB-011), and that any expiry/recovery action is safe across reconnect and shutdown. Capacity supervision runs only after awaited cleanup/calibration/inventory work (head lines 63–81); determine whether its timing is merely diagnostic/recovery or security-critical, and whether authoritative admission expiry remains independent of this cadence (T-053/T-057, A-018). Missing helper evidence is a material coverage limit, not proof of a missing control. These integration questions require further source review, not vulnerability findings.
